Treat exact reproduction of all retained pairs as a hard gate: do not submit a test prediction from an unvalidated candidate, even if its transform runs successfully. If a submission is incorrect, first re-run the exact submitted program and compare it against those fixtures; do not make another guess until its demo mismatches and the alternative rule's differing predictions are explicit. Request another demo only if it can distinguish live hypotheses; requests and wrong submissions cost score. First identify the structural layout from the examples: horizontal/vertical separators, panel boundaries, repeated motif pitch, and the actual coordinates/colors sampled for the output. Reproduce at least two demos with different grid sizes before accepting a coordinate rule; do not infer the output by eyeballing the test alone. If the failed candidate came from a cached program and no demos are available, request a demo before editing or trying another prediction; a repeated run or unchanged rewrite of that candidate adds no evidence. After repeated failures, pause before another attempt: state the competing hypotheses, identify evidence in demos that distinguishes them, and test the full candidate against all retained pairs. Treat feedback saying an output is not a valid grid as an output-format/serialization failure first: verify outer type, dimensions, row lengths, and integer range against the stated constraints; do not infer a puzzle-rule failure until those checks pass. If demos leave competing rules, make each candidate predict the complete outputs for every retained pair and compare the cells that differ between hypotheses; spend another demo only when its possible result would choose between them. After the demo cap, if no candidate reproduces all demos, keep the uncertainty explicit and do not turn an unsupported guess into a claimed validated rule; choose another attempt only when the retained evidence supports it. Do not edit the task file to an unvalidated candidate.

 "content": "def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # Solid lines split the canvas into panels. Copy the distinctive panel's
    # non-background pattern into the remaining panels at matching offsets.
    sep = None
    for color in set(v for row in grid for v in row):
        if any(all(v == color for v in row) for row in grid) or any(
            all(grid[r][c] == color for r in range(h)) for c in range(w)):
            sep = color
            break
    if sep is None:
        return [row[:] for row in grid]
    rs = [r for r in range(h) if all(v == sep for v in grid[r])]
    cs = [c for c in range(w) if all(grid[r][c] == sep for r in range(h))]
    rstarts, rends = [0] + [r+1 for r in rs], rs + [h]
    cstarts, cends = [0] + [c+1 for c in cs], cs + [w]
    panels = [(a,b,c,d) for a,b in zip(rstarts,rends) for c,d in zip(cstarts,cends)]
    # Background is the most frequent color other than the separator.
    from collections import Counter
    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row if v != sep)
    bg = counts.most_common(1)[0][0]
    source = max(panels, key=lambda p: sum(grid[r][c] != bg and grid[r][c] != sep
                    for r in range(p[0],p[1]) for c in range(p[2],p[3])))
    a,b,c,d = source
    pattern = [(r-a, col-c, grid[r][col]) for r in range(a,b) for col in range(c,d)
               if grid[r][col] != bg and grid[r][col] != sep]
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    for y0,y1,x0,x1 in panels:
        if (y0,y1,x0,x1) == source:
            continue
        for dy,dx,v in pattern:
            if y0+dy < y1 and x0+dx < x1 and out[y0+dy][x0+dx] == bg:
                out[y0+dy][x0+dx] = v
    return out
"
}
